key_insight: A scalable framework that enables humanoid robots to perform robust hiking and parkour in unstructured environments by combining a local, drift-tolerant exteroceptive perception stream with hierarchical locomotion control, avoiding reliance on full mapping or fragile end-to-end training.
problem_solved: Integrates exteroception into humanoid locomotion without falling prey to mapping-based state-estimation drift or torso-jitter failures, and without the scalability and complexity issues of prior end-to-end approaches.
method: Ego-centric, local perceptual representation (vision/LiDAR fusion) designed to be resilient to state-estimation drift and torso jitter, avoiding dense global maps.
Hierarchical control: perception-driven footstep/trajectory planning at a higher level + robust low-level stabilizing controllers for contact-aware execution.
Scalable training and deployment pipeline (simulation curriculum, domain randomization and modular transfer) that reduces sample complexity and supports real-world transfer.
impact: Enables practical, scalable deployment of perceptive humanoid locomotion in real-world, unstructured environments and provides a modular template for research on perception-action integration and hierarchical controllers in robotics.
